Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.

Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.

methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 26th-27th March 2025
Sample: 1,544 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.
Data were collected, analysed and weighted by BMG Research.

methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 6th - 8th May 2025
Sample: 1,525 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. methodology_text:
Freshwater Strategy Polling Results

Sample: 1,260 UK adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of UK voters. Targets were Age-Sex, Education, Region, 2024 General Election and the 2016 EU Referendum results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base vote intentions are produced for GB only, 'lean' responses are included, remaining undecideds are removed to produce a 'valid' result, then finally results are filtered for 9 or 10 LTV.

Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a likert scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.

headline_definition_text: Base: Not sure and prefer not to say removed
methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 24th - 25th June 2025
Sample: 1,617 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.
Data were collected, analysed and weighted by BMG Research.

methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 29th - 31st July 2025
Sample: 1,528 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.

methodology_text:
Freshwater Strategy Polling Results
Fieldwork dates: 3 - 5 October 2025
Sample: 1,251 UK adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of UK voters. Targets were Age-Sex, Education, Region, 2024 General Election and the 2016 EU Referendum results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base vote intentions are produced for GB only, 'lean' responses are included, remaining undecideds are removed to produce a 'valid' result, then finally results are filtered for 9 or 10 LTV.
Margin of Error: For a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result. This poll will have a MoE of approximately 2.8%.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a likert scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.
Data were collected, analysed and weighted by Freshwater Strategy.

methodology_text:
Freshwater Strategy Polling Results
Fieldwork dates: 7 - 9 November 2025
Sample: 1,250 UK adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of UK voters. Targets were Age-Sex, Education, Region, 2024 General Election and the 2016 EU Referendum results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base vote intentions are produced for GB only, 'lean' responses are included, remaining undecideds are removed to produce a 'valid' result, then finally results are filtered for 9 or 10 LTV.
Margin of Error: For a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result. This poll will have a MoE of approximately 2.8%.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a likert scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.
Data were collected, analysed and weighted by Freshwater Strategy.

BMG Polling results

Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.

methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 25th-26th March 2026
Sample: 1,507 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.

methodology_text:
Freshwater Strategy Polling Results
Fieldwork dates: 10 – 12 April 2026
Sample: 1,250 UK adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.

Voting Intention Adjustments: After base vote intentions are produced for GB only, 'lean' responses are included, remaining undecideds are removed to produce a 'valid' result, then finally results are filtered for 9 or 10 LTV.

Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a likert scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.

methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 29th-30th April 2026
Sample: 1,521 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.

methodology_text:
BMG Polling results
Fieldwork dates: 26th-28th May 2026
Sample: 1,511 GB adults aged 18+
Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information. Responses such as “Other”, “Don't know” and “Refused” are not usually randomised.
Data were collected, analysed and weighted by BMG Research.

BMG Polling results

Data Collection Method: Fieldwork was conducted online. Invitations to participate were sent to members of online panels. Non-response from different demographic groups was taken into account during the fieldwork phase and post-fieldwork adjustments.
Weighting: Results were weighted to reflect the profile of GB adults. Targets were Age/Sex, Parliamentary Constituency, Indices of Multiple Deprivation (IMD), Education, the 2024 General Election results and the 2016 EU Referendum results. All targets are based on Official Statistics from the ONS that are awarded National Statistics status, as well as the BBC's published election results.
Voting Intention Adjustments: After base weights BMG performs an additional step to arrive at it's final voting intention figure - squeeze responses are re-allocated and given a weighting factor of 0.75. Where no party is selected at squeeze question a factor of 0.5 is allocated based on how they previously voted in 2024 General Election.
Electoral Registration Adjustment:  Factors have been applied to the electoral voting intention figures using to account for rates of electoral registration among key groups. Factors were derived from a survey question that asked respondents whether or not they are registered to vote. The results were then segmented by age and tenure (two variables that were identified by the Electoral Commission report “Accuracy & Completeness of Electoral Registers 2016” as key discriminators of registration completeness).
Margin of Error: As a sample of the population was interviewed, the results are subject to a margin of error around various estimates. This means that, given the random nature of the sampling process, we can be confident that the actual result lies somewhere within the margin of error. For example, with a sample of 1,000 we can be 95% certain that the actual value will fall 3% either side of the result.
Questions & Presentation: All results are shown in full in this spreadsheet, in order, and using the wording that was put to respondents. For questions where the list of responses is names of parties, names or statements, these will typically have been displayed to respondents in a random order, but are ordered in this spreadsheet. Questions typically not shown in a random order are those where there is a natural or accepted order to maintain i.e. a scale from “strongly agree” to “strongly disagree”, a list of numbers from 0 to 10, or questions that have a factual, rather than opinion-related answer, such as key demographic information.
